findings.issue: The wrapper hides only X-Forwarded-For. Spring's ForwardedHeaderFilter builds the remote address with ForwardedHeaderUtils.parseForwardedFor, which reads the RFC 7239 'Forwarded' header first. A request with 'Forwarded: for=9.9.9.9' and no X-Internal-Client-Ip therefore still gets getRemoteAddr()=9.9.9.9, and ClientIp's socket-peer fallback is again attacker-chosen (login throttle key, device record, admin audit). This is the same reachability as round-1 minor 1: direct in-cluster or VPC callers, or the gateway removing X-Internal-Client-Ip when the peer cannot be resolved. Whether SCG 5.0.2 drops an inbound Forwarded header without trusted-proxies is not shown anywhere in the repo. The new docs and ADR line 49 say 'the remote address is always the socket peer', which overstates the fix. Header case is handled correctly: equalsIgnoreCase covers getHeader, getHeaders and getHeaderNames, and ServletServerHttpRequest builds its HttpHeaders from those methods.
findings.fix: Hide 'Forwarded' as well as X-Forwarded-For in WithoutXff, for example with a case-insensitive Set.of("x-forwarded-for","forwarded"). Host and Proto still come from X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto, which is what the ALB and CloudFront send. Add a test where 'Forwarded: for=9.9.9.9' (mixed case too) still gives getRemoteAddr()==socket peer, and a test with lower-case 'x-forwarded-for'.

findings.issue: Boot's own registration, which this bean replaces, calls setDispatcherTypes(REQUEST, ASYNC, ERROR) and applies ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer (relative redirects). The replacement keeps the default REQUEST dispatch only and no customizer. This is not a security weakness: ERROR and ASYNC dispatches see the raw socket peer. But error and async paths lose the public Host and Proto, so the OIDC behaviour can differ from what framework mode gave before.
findings.fix: Add registration.setDispatcherTypes(DispatcherType.REQUEST, DispatcherType.ASYNC, DispatcherType.ERROR) to match Boot. Optionally apply any ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer beans via ObjectProvider.

findings.issue: AuditInterceptor is auto-configured in every servlet service. Only the gateway, payment and user-service are pinned to none, and only auth is filtered. The other services keep Boot's Kubernetes default, native: Tomcat RemoteIpValve trusts XFF from internal-range peers. Their audit-IP fallback, used when X-Internal-Client-Ip is absent, can therefore still come from a client-supplied XFF. This is audit-only and limited to in-cluster or fallback paths, which are inside the stated ClusterIP trust boundary. It contradicts the docs' general statement.
findings.fix: Either set SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for all non-auth services in the Helm template, as a default with auth as the exception, or narrow the doc and ADR wording to name the services that are pinned.

summary: Delta b4abf171..690f934a. The auth ForwardedHeaderConfig correctly replaces Boot's framework ForwardedHeaderFilter. The CEO's evidence from the Boot 4.0.7 source shows Boot backs off under @ConditionalOnMissingFilterBean(ForwardedHeaderFilter.class), and this bean is a FilterRegistrationBean of a ForwardedHeaderFilter subclass. The bean hides X-Forwarded-For in any header case from getHeader, getHeaders and getHeaderNames, so an XFF can no longer become getRemoteAddr(). X-Forwarded-Host and X-Forwarded-Proto still pass through for the OIDC callback, and the tests cover both. One gap remains: the RFC 7239 'Forwarded: for=' header still sets the remote address. It is reachable only by in-cluster callers or on the gateway fallback path, so it stays minor, as in round 1. Pinning payment-service to none is safe. Payment builds no URLs from request host or scheme, and its per-IP key comes from X-Internal-Client-Ip with the real socket peer as fallback. Round-1 minors: minor 2 (stale docs in env-descriptions.json, environment-variables.md and the user-service application.yml comment) is resolved. Minor 3 (ADR B-4 gate now covers all four consumers) is resolved. Minor 1 is mostly resolved, apart from the Forwarded header. The delta adds no new endpoints, secrets, PII logging, ledger changes or dependencies. Approve with three minor findings.
